endorsements.quote: Clinician involvement throughout the multimodal clinical AI development pipeline is therefore essential—to guide model design, construction, development, deployment, and iterative refinement.

Clinician involvement is thus essential in the earliest planning stages of clinical AI deployment, both to ensure that tools are easy to use and meeting genuine clinical needs, as well as to educate users of the benefits.

unlisted_practices: Involve clinicians as codevelopers throughout the entire multimodal AI development pipeline, not only at deployment.
Involve clinicians in data collection, data labelling, and data processing to advise on data quality, bias, and the validity of processing assumptions.
Design multimodal clinical AI to support decisions when some data modalities are missing and to reflect the personalised, hierarchical order of clinical data acquisition.
Involve clinicians in monitoring for dataset drift and shift, including decisions on when to pause the model, how much data to collect, and what data to use for retraining.
Involve clinicians in developing uncertainty quantification and explainability measures so they are fit for purpose for clinical oversight.
Consult a wide range of clinicians with differing seniority and experience when deploying multimodal AI.
Establish actively managed multidisciplinary communities of clinicians and AI developers, using research community managers.
Embed AI developers as observing members of clinical multidisciplinary teams to deepen their understanding of clinical workflows.
Funding bodies should stipulate an expectation of clinician involvement throughout AI development.
Train clinician-scientists with both computational and clinical expertise and educate healthcare professionals about AI.
Keep AI tools up to date with evolving clinical guidelines through ongoing clinical engagement.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary article arguing for clinician involvement throughout the development pipeline of multimodal AI tools.
